title: Wolverines' quiet last choruses and rocking rhythm
summary: Ashcraft remembers the Wolverines at the Green Mill getting softer through the last choruses while the room rocked.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: The, uh, one, one phenomenon that's gone. That, that I hate to see go. Was the effect the, the Wolverines used to have. They'd play 15 last choruses or something. Uh, I can remember it at the, uh, Green Mill. Where the, the, uh, the, the first, the first ensemble at the end of the tune would be a, a good, solid, powerful, pretty loud one. And they'd get progressively softer. And they would never play a loud one at the end as they would now. If they played a soft one. That's right. And they'd play right out to a point where the whole joint was rocking. Uh, but rocking from tempo and you could hardly hear them.

And the more dancers, the more, of course, the dance, uh, the sound of the dancing itself would meld into it. Bix used to play often with it. And Jimmy did the same thing. He'd play with his horn between his knees. And they would just get into a rocking thing. I think the only record they ever made where you can visualize it a little bit is Tijuana. Where it's just a solid thing all the way through. But that, that, getting, getting really down.
